subject: History
topic: Gandhian Movements — Champaran, Kheda, Dandi March
description: Gandhi's early Indian campaigns: Champaran Satyagraha 1917, Kheda Satyagraha 1918, Dandi Salt March 1930 — causes, outcomes, significance.

questions.stem: The Champaran Satyagraha (1917) was Gandhi's first major civil disobedience movement in India. It was launched against:

options.option_text: The 'tinkathia' system forcing peasants to grow indigo on 3/20 of their land for British planters
The salt tax imposed by the British on coastal salt production in Bihar (not this)
The zamindari system that collected exorbitant land revenue from peasants in Bihar
The British ban on native cotton textile production in the Champaran region (not this)

questions.explanation: CHAMPARAN SATYAGRAHA (1917): CAUSE — the TINKATHIA system (also written Teen-kathia): indigo planters in Champaran (Bihar) forced peasants to cultivate INDIGO on 3/20 (three-twentieths) of their land. With synthetic indigo replacing natural indigo in world markets, planters demanded peasants pay compensation for early release from the tinkathia obligation — called LAGAAN or TAWAN — at extortionate rates. GANDHI'S ROLE: Rajkumar Shukla (a peasant leader) persuaded Gandhi to visit Champaran. Gandhi reached Motihari (April 1917). British authorities ordered him to leave; he REFUSED — first act of civil disobedience in India. Government eventually set up an inquiry commission; Gandhi himself served on it. OUTCOME: Champaran Agrarian Act 1918 abolished tinkathia system. SIGNIFICANCE: First successful application of Satyagraha in India; Nehru said it was 'the beginning of a new era.' TAGORE called Gandhi 'MAHATMA' for this work (one account). UPSC ANGLE: Champaran appears in UPSC Prelims and Mains GS-1 (Modern India) every alternate cycle. PYQ FREQUENCY: SSC CGL, IBPS PO, UPSC Prelims — Champaran facts (year, cause, location) 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: The Dandi March (1930) covered approximately 385 km from Sabarmati Ashram (Ahmedabad) to Dandi (Gujarat) in how many days?

options.option_text: 24 days (12 March to 5 April 1930)
12 days (half the actual duration)
36 days (longer estimate sometimes cited)
48 days (full two months estimate)

questions.explanation: DANDI MARCH: 12 March 1930 → 5 April 1930 = 24 days. Gandhi walked ~385 km from SABARMATI ASHRAM (Ahmedabad) to DANDI (coastal village, Navsari district, Gujarat). Started with 78 followers; grew to tens of thousands as people joined. DANDI (5 April): Gandhi picked up a lump of salt from the seashore — symbolically breaking the SALT LAW (British monopoly on salt production and trade). SALT LAWS: British forbade Indians from producing or possessing salt except through government channels. Heavy tax and monopoly profits. AFTERMATH: April 6 onwards = mass salt-making all over India. Gandhi arrested on 5 May 1930. Simon Commission reaction: British arrested ~80,000 people. DHARASANA SATYAGRAHA: Sarojini Naidu led the raid on Dharasana salt works (May 1930) — thousands beaten by British police — reported by American journalist Webb Miller, creating international outrage. UPSC ANGLE: Dandi March was the trigger for the Civil Disobedience Movement (CDM). First Round Table Conference (November 1930) — Congress boycotted (Gandhi in jail). Gandhi-Irwin Pact (1931) — CDM suspended. PYQ FREQUENCY: dates and facts of Dandi March appear in almost every exam — SSC CGL, IBPS PO, RRB NTPC, UPSC.

questions.stem: The Kheda Satyagraha (1918) was a campaign against tax collection by the British. The peasants of Kheda (Gujarat) demanded:

options.option_text: Suspension of land revenue collection since crops had failed and the district qualified for remission under revenue rules
Abolition of the indigo plantation system in Kheda like Champaran (not this) instead however alone
Reduction in salt taxes affecting coastal communities in Kheda (not this) instead however alone
Release of political prisoners held under the Rowlatt Act in Kheda jails (not this) instead however

questions.explanation: KHEDA SATYAGRAHA (1918): Cause — crops failed in Kheda (Gujarat) due to FAMINE and floods. Revenue rules stated that if yield was below 25% of the normal, land revenue should be REMITTED (waived). Peasants claimed they qualified; British refused to verify and demanded full tax payment. GANDHI + SARDAR VALLABHBHAI PATEL (first major political role) organised the campaign — peasants refused to pay tax. Government finally agreed: landless/poor peasants would not be coerced; better-off peasants would pay. SIGNIFICANCE: (1) First major use of Satyagraha by Gandhi in Gujarat. (2) VALLABHBHAI PATEL emerged as a nationalist leader here — earned the title 'Sardar' (leader) through later work. (3) Model for farmer-tax refusals. KHEDA vs CHAMPARAN: Champaran = indigo planters vs peasants. Kheda = revenue collection by British. ROWLATT ACT (1919): anti-sedition act passed after Kheda — different issue and year. PYQ FREQUENCY: Kheda Satyagraha and Sardar Patel connection appears in UPSC Prelims, SSC CGL, state PSCs 1× per cycle. EXAM TRAP: confuse Kheda (Gujarat, 1918, land revenue) with Champaran (Bihar, 1917, indigo).

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about the Civil Disobedience Movement (1930-34) is INCORRECT?

options.option_text: The Nehru Report (1928) provided the constitutional blueprint that triggered the CDM
Gandhi launched the CDM with the Dandi Salt March in March 1930 (not this)
Gandhi-Irwin Pact (1931) suspended the CDM after negotiations (not this)
Congress boycotted the First Round Table Conference (1930) (not this)

questions.explanation: INCORRECT STATEMENT: The NEHRU REPORT (1928) was a constitutional proposal by a Congress committee (chaired by Motilal Nehru) — it was a response to the Simon Commission (which excluded Indians). It did NOT trigger the CDM. The triggers for CDM were: (1) Simon Commission (1927) — all-British committee, Indian boycott. (2) Declaration of PURNA SWARAJ (Complete Independence) at Lahore Congress session (December 1929, presided by Jawaharlal Nehru). (3) Gandhi's Eleven Demands (January 1930) sent as ultimatum to Viceroy Irwin — including abolition of salt tax. Irwin's refusal → Dandi March. CORRECT STATEMENTS in options: ✓ Dandi Salt March (March 1930) started CDM. ✓ Gandhi-Irwin Pact (5 March 1931) — CDM suspended; Gandhi attended Second RTC; government released political prisoners. ✓ Congress boycotted First RTC (November 1930). UPSC ANGLE: The CDM sequence — Declaration of Purna Swaraj → Dandi March → Civil Disobedience → Gandhi-Irwin Pact → Second RTC → CDM resumed 1932 → Third RTC → Communal Award → Poona Pact — is a frequently tested UPSC narrative. PYQ FREQUENCY: CDM sequence and events in UPSC Prelims, SSC CGL 2-3× per decade.

questions.stem: Vaikom Satyagraha (1924-25) in Kerala was unique among Gandhian movements because it was directed against:

options.option_text: The ban on lower-caste Hindus using public roads near the Vaikom temple (temple-entry and anti-untouchability focus)
British taxation of toddy-tappers in Travancore region of Kerala (not this) instead however
The ban on reading vernacular newspapers under the Vernacular Press Act (not this) instead
The refusal of Travancore rulers to introduce adult franchise in the state (not this) instead

questions.explanation: VAIKOM SATYAGRAHA (1924-25): Organised in TRAVANCORE (now Kerala) by T.K. Madhavan and K.P. Kesava Menon. CAUSE: Public roads around the Vaikom (Mahadeva) temple were FORBIDDEN to lower-caste Hindus (Ezhavas, Pulayas). Protesters peacefully walked on the roads despite bans. Gandhi visited Vaikom in March 1925 — key intervention. Satyagraha ended when Travancore government agreed to open THREE out of four roads around the temple to all people. The fourth road (nearest the temple) was opened only after the full TEMPLE ENTRY PROCLAMATION of Travancore (1936). SIGNIFICANCE: (1) First major Satyagraha focused on SOCIAL REFORM (not against British but against caste discrimination by Hindu society). (2) E.V. Ramasamy Periyar (EVR) participated — later founded Dravidian movement. (3) Paved way for Travancore Temple Entry Proclamation (12 November 1936). UPSC ANGLE: Vaikom and temple-entry movements are tested in UPSC Prelims as part of 'social reform movements.' It shows Satyagraha was applied against Indian social evils, not just British colonialism. PYQ FREQUENCY: Vaikom Satyagraha facts in UPSC Prelims, KPSC, TNPSC 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: The Dharasana Salt Works Raid (May 1930) — a dramatic episode in the Civil Disobedience Movement — was led by whom after Gandhi's arrest?

options.option_text: Sarojini Naidu (with Abbas Tyabji initially), after Gandhi was arrested on 5 May 1930
Jawaharlal Nehru (who led the CDM while Gandhi was in jail) (not this)
Subhas Chandra Bose (who took over CDM leadership from Gandhi) (not this)
Vallabhbhai Patel (who was Gandhi's closest associate in Gujarat campaigns)

questions.explanation: DHARASANA RAID (21 May 1930): Gandhi was arrested 5 May 1930 at Karadi. He had designated ABBAS TYABJI (elderly Congress leader) to lead the Dharasana raid. Tyabji was also arrested before the march. SAROJINI NAIDU then led ~2,500 volunteers to the Dharasana salt works. British police beat them with steel-tipped lathis; volunteers walked silently into the blows without retaliating. American journalist WEBB MILLER's eyewitness report — published in 1,350 newspapers worldwide — created massive international sympathy for India's cause. SIGNIFICANCE: Dramatised the non-violent resistance; exposed British brutality to the world. JAWAHARLAL NEHRU: was leading other aspects of CDM but was also arrested (April 1930). SUBHAS BOSE: not involved in CDM leadership in this way. PATEL: arrested early in the CDM. UPSC ANGLE: Dharasana Raid is tested in UPSC Prelims as an underappreciated episode in Indian freedom struggle. Sarojini Naidu = 'Nightingale of India' (for poetry) + CDM leader. PYQ FREQUENCY: Dharasana raid leader in UPSC Prelims, UPPSC, MPSC 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: The Champaran Agrarian Enquiry Committee (1917), formed after Gandhi's intervention, submitted a report that led to the abolition of the tinkathia system. An important aspect of this process was that Gandhi:

options.option_text: Served as a member of the committee himself — an unusual colonial arrangement of including the protest leader in the official inquiry
Was deported back to South Africa before the committee could submit its report (not this) instead however
Refused to participate in any government-appointed body and organised parallel hearings (not this) instead
Was imprisoned throughout the enquiry period and participated only through written submissions (not this)

questions.explanation: UNIQUE ASPECT of Champaran (1917): After Gandhi's arrival and the initial confrontation with authorities (ordered to leave, refused), the Lieutenant Governor of Bihar set up an ENQUIRY COMMITTEE. GANDHI WAS APPOINTED A MEMBER of this official enquiry committee — an extraordinary colonial concession. He collected testimonies from thousands of peasants about tinkathia oppression. The committee's report supported peasants' complaints → Champaran Agrarian Act (1918) → abolished tinkathia. SIGNIFICANCE: (1) Showed British could be moved through Satyagraha to make official concessions. (2) Gandhi's inclusion on an official body was unprecedented for a protest leader. (3) Data-collection approach — Gandhi insisted on documented evidence, not just agitation — became a model. CONTRAST: In later movements (CDM, Quit India), British were less willing to include Congress leaders in official processes. UPSC ANGLE: Champaran's resolution through an official inquiry (not just agitation) is a key lesson in constitutional methods + Satyagraha combination. BIPIN CHANDRA in 'India's Struggle for Independence' emphasises this administrative concession as a turning point. PYQ FREQUENCY: Gandhi's role in the Champaran committee — UPSC Prelims, UPPSC 1× per decade; high differentiator question.
